title: Finite cohomological dimension of finite-type morphisms
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $K$-morphism between
schemes of finite type over $K$, with their structure morphisms and compatibility
as in [def-weil-scheme-over-base].

1. **(1)** $\kuncd(f)<\infty$.
1. **(2)** If $K$ is separably
closed, then $\kuncd(X)<\infty$ for every scheme $X$ of finite type
over $K$.

Clause (1) and clause (2) are the classical finiteness of the
cohomological dimension of a scheme of finite type over a field, which
this manuscript already imports elsewhere: the finiteness chain of
the constructibility chapter uses it in \texttt{sbc-thm-finiteness-finite-type}, and
the Jacobian chapter proves the curve case in
lem:sc-cohomological-dimension, so that the curve and proper
instances are internal to the blueprint. The affine bound
$\kuncd(X)\le\kuncd(K)+\kundim X$ for affine $X$ of finite type over
$K$, which is Tag [0F0V](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0V)
of the Stacks Project, is not needed in this chapter.
(*Source:* Stacks Project, Lemma 59.96.2,
[Tag `0F10`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F10), in
Section 59.96 (finite cohomological dimension): clause (1) is assertion
(1) of that lemma, and clause (2) is
its assertion (2) — which assumes $\kuncd(K)<\infty$ — combined with
\texttt{lem-kun-cd-sep-closed-point}, where the cohomological dimension of a
separably closed point is computed to be $0$.) In the Stacks Project the proof uses the induction principle of
Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 30.4.1,
[Tag `08DR`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08DR),
with the affine cases Lemma 59.95.8,
[Tag `0F0X`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0X), for
clause (1) and Proposition 59.95.6,
[Tag `0F0V`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F0V), for
clause (2), together with the Mayer–Vietoris sequences Lemma 59.50.2,
[Tag `0EYK`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EYK), and
Lemma 59.50.1, [Tag
`0A50`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A50).

proof.text: Finite-type structure maps give a compact source and Noetherian, hence quasi-separated, schemes. Choose a natural n bounding the dimensions of all field extensions of X. For each torsion abelian sheaf, the uniform higher-image theorem gives vanishing in every integer degree above 2n. Thus 2n lies in the set defining the morphism cohomological dimension. The defining infimum is at most this finite number, so it is below infinity.

If K is separably closed, choose a natural d bounding dim X. The existing source finite-type torsion cohomology theorem with field bound zero gives Subsingleton (Sheaf.H F q) for every torsion F and q>2d. The natural Ext/derived global-sections comparison transports this to the predicate used by the numerical scheme dimension. Its infimum is therefore at most 2d, hence finite. Empty schemes are included throughout.

statement_change.what: The phrase morphism between finite-type K-schemes left compatibility with the K-structure maps ambiguous. The first Lean statement omitted it entirely. Specify a K-morphism, as required by the proof of Stacks 0F10 via 0F0X: its affine closed-immersion diagram into affine spaces over K commutes only for K-morphisms. This clarifies the source meaning rather than replacing it with an unrelated finiteness assumption. The two theorem names in the unchanged provenance explanation are rendered as text rather than bracketed statement-dependency citations; they do not introduce notions needed to type the statement.
